clue.text: Composed when seated for a change

indicators.note: the letters of the word seated are changed around, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone feels calmer once they sit down for a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' is the anagram signal: SEATED is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A composed person is calm and unruffled, which is what sedate describes.

clue.text: Stint? What solver needs to do

definitions.meaning: a period of work or duty
write out the letters of the answer correctly

explanation.definitionFit: A shift of work is one sense, and forming words from letters is what a crossword solver must do.

clue.text: Having lost half, region's aim — to expand

indicators.note: having lost half says the region word keeps only its front half

parts.note: a district is a region
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A region, having lost half its territory, aims to expand.
explanation.walkthrough: DISTRICT loses half its letters to leave DIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell outwards, which is a way of expanding.

clue.text: Story showed no interest when told, It's well down on delivery

indicators.note: when told means the words are spoken and heard as similar ones

parts.note: a tale is a story; being bored is showing no interest

explanation.surface: Someone tells a dull story; a delivery van appears.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on a lorry's hinged rear flap, lowered well down when goods are delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinged board at the back of a truck drops down to unload goods.

clue.text: A doctor with paper including one off course

indicators.note: the string built from a, doctor and paper takes the next piece within it

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A doctor carrying a newspaper with someone who has wandered off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' places the one inside the doctor-and-paper string, just after the doctor; the FT is the Financial Times, which sets this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat drifting with no steering has gone off course, the sense of adrift.

clue.text: This clue is exceptionally wordy. It's a gift

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests the letters of wordy are arranged unusually

explanation.surface: A solver complains this clue is very long-winded.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's family traditionally gave property to the groom on marriage, a marriage gift.

clue.text: City in ruins, perhaps isolated

indicators.note: in places the city within the ruins
perhaps suggests the combined letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A city lying in ruins may be cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' is not Ur or another ancient ruin here; the Los Angeles letters are added to the ruins before 'perhaps' rearranges all seven.
explanation.definitionFit: Island-like and cut off from others is the sense of this word.

clue.text: Being self-restrained, fit of rage consumed

parts.note: a temper is an angry outburst
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A self-controlled person still loses it in an outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate describes moderation and self-control.

clue.text: To start the journey the groups feel unwell

parts.note: sets are groups of things
to ail is to be sick

explanation.surface: Travellers about to set off find that some of the party feel ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting sail is when a ship departs, so it marks the beginning of a voyage.

clue.text: Dreaded: one with terrible woes and complaint

parts.note: A is one, as in 'a book'

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters of woes are put into a mangled order

parts.note: ME, myalgic encephalomyelitis, is an illness or complaint

explanation.surface: Someone dreads their troubles and an illness on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreaded' fits the older sense of awe as fear, not the modern 'brilliant'; 'terrible' scrambles only the woes.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesome in its older sense means inspiring awe or fear, so something dreaded.

clue.text: Turkey -a bird with insect endlessly quivering

parts.note: TR is the international code for Turkey
the emu is a large flightless bird

indicators.note: endlessly means the insect word loses its final letter

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect

explanation.surface: A turkey shivers with an insect on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremulous means trembling or shaking.

clue.text: English line on classic about stray source of wine

indicators.note: about means the race name goes around the next piece

parts.note: the Derby is one of the English Classic horse races
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A horse-racing story about a stray runner in a classic race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is one of five British flat races called the Classics; 'about' puts the straying inside the race name, before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderberries are fermented to make a country wine, so the fruit is a wine's raw material.

clue.text: The song told a story

definitions.meaning: a German art song for voice and piano

explanation.definitionFit: A Schubert-style German art song carries this name, and telling a story is a childish euphemism for fibbing.

clue.text: Means of communication aimed indiscriminately

indicators.note: indiscriminately suggests the letters of aimed are scattered at random

explanation.surface: Communication methods are aimed at people without discrimination.
explanation.definitionFit: Press, radio and television are the channels for communicating with the public.

clue.text: New wine with hot meal at the same time

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: Drinking new wine with a hot meal simultaneously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges WINE, H and MEAL together.
explanation.definitionFit: This adverb means during the same period, simultaneously.

clue.text: Meaningful stuff

definitions.meaning: relevant or significant, as with evidence

explanation.definitionFit: Evidence that matters is called relevant in this sense, and cloth or substance is the second sense.

clue.text: Have impact on actor's words at side of play

parts.note: to touch is to affect
an actor speaks lines

explanation.surface: An actor's speech affects the audience at the side of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The play here is a game on a pitch, not a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: The boundary marking the side of a football or rugby pitch.

clue.text: Hand finally laid off after trouble in the plant

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word hand
the words laid off are put through trouble, i.e. jumbled

explanation.surface: A worker made redundant has trouble in the factory plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' reads as a factory with laid-off workers, but it is a flower; 'after trouble' jumbles the seven letters of laid off.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow spring flower is a bulb plant of the narcissus family.

clue.text: Cargo boat not about to become combatant

indicators.note: not means the about word is dropped from the boat word

parts.note: a freighter carries cargo
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A cargo ship that is not about to become a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A combatant is one who takes part in a battle.

clue.text: Bob, perhaps, difficult to follow misses the last two

indicators.note: misses the last two means the final pair of letters is dropped

parts.note: something unclear is hard to follow

explanation.surface: A man called Bob is hard to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob's your uncle' is a British phrase meaning 'and there you are', so Bob is an example relative.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase makes Bob the archetypal relative of this kind, a parent's brother.

clue.text: Draw together for an intimate description

definitions.meaning: to come nearer as a group, narrowing gaps
a detailed close portrait, like a near camera shot

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means to bunch or narrow together; as a noun, a detailed shot or account.

clue.text: Society to rate the big swallow?

parts.note: to rate someone, like to wig them, is to scold them

explanation.surface: A society meets to rank the largest swallow, a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Rate and wig both mean to tell off, old-fashioned British senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A large gulp of drink is called a swig.

clue.text: H-Hugo upset in run-out, to employ bad behaviour

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the other pieces

parts.note: R is run and O is out, cricket scoring abbreviations
to use is to employ

indicators.note: upset means the letters of H-Hugo are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A cricketer named Hugo is upset to be run out and behaves badly.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scoring R is run and O is out; 'upset' scrambles H-Hugo and 'in' sits the result between run-out and to employ.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdy, violent horseplay is the sense here, a kind of misconduct.

clue.text: Managed the central heating in the farm

parts.note: ran means managed
CH is the abbreviation for central heating

explanation.surface: Someone controlled the heating on the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A large livestock farm in America is a ranch.

clue.text: Support parade

definitions.meaning: a brace or prop in a structure

explanation.definitionFit: A brace in a frame is one sense; walking proudly showing off is the other.

clue.text: Getting place about time when meal is served

indicators.note: about means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: siting something is getting it a location

explanation.surface: Getting a seat in time for the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dining sitting is one of the scheduled times at which a meal is served to a group.

clue.text: Listener in company could be discharged

indicators.note: in places the listener inside the company

parts.note: a firm is a business or company
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: An eavesdropper in a business might be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharged' suggests being fired from a job, which fits the company surface, but here it means fired as a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun is something that may be fired, i.e. discharged.

clue.text: Unrefined, worldly (not a beginner)

indicators.note: not says the beginner is left out of the word

parts.note: worldly means of this world, earthly
L stands for learner, a beginner, from L-plates

explanation.surface: Someone is crude and worldly, but no novice.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse or crude humour is described as down-to-earth in this sense.

clue.text: The oppressor to get rid of the blemish!

parts.note: de- is a prefix meaning remove, as in de-ice
a spot is a blemish

explanation.surface: Someone tries to remove a spot from the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: To de-spot would be to rid of spots.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant rules oppressively, the meaning of despot.
